  2935→/* Implementation of -Wmultistatement-macros.  This warning warns about
  2936→   cases when a macro expands to multiple statements not wrapped in
  2937→   do {} while (0) or ({ }) and is used as a body of if/else/for/while
  2938→   conditionals.  For example,
  2939→
  2940→   #define DOIT x++; y++
  2941→
  2942→   if (c)
  2943→     DOIT;
  2944→
  2945→   will increment y unconditionally.
  2946→
  2947→   BODY_LOC is the location of the first token in the body after labels
  2948→   have been parsed, NEXT_LOC is the location of the next token after the
  2949→   body of the conditional has been parsed, and GUARD_LOC is the location
  2950→   of the conditional.  */
  2951→
  2952→void
  2953→warn_for_multistatement_macros (location_t body_loc, location_t next_loc,
  2954→				location_t guard_loc, enum rid keyword)
  2955→{
  2956→  if (!warn_multistatement_macros)
  2957→    return;
  2958→
  2959→  /* Ain't got time to waste.  We only care about macros here.  */
  2960→  if (!from_macro_expansion_at (body_loc)
  2961→      || !from_macro_expansion_at (next_loc))
  2962→    return;
  2963→
  2964→  /* Let's skip macros defined in system headers.  */
  2965→  if (in_system_header_at (body_loc)
  2966→      || in_system_header_at (next_loc))
  2967→    return;
  2968→
  2969→  /* Find the actual tokens in the macro definition.  BODY_LOC and
  2970→     NEXT_LOC have to come from the same spelling location, but they
  2971→     will resolve to different locations in the context of the macro
  2972→     definition.  */
  2973→  location_t body_loc_exp
  2974→    = linemap_resolve_location (line_table, body_loc,
  2975→				LRK_MACRO_DEFINITION_LOCATION, NULL);
  2976→  location_t next_loc_exp
  2977→    = linemap_resolve_location (line_table, next_loc,
  2978→				LRK_MACRO_DEFINITION_LOCATION, NULL);
  2979→  location_t guard_loc_exp
  2980→    = linemap_resolve_location (line_table, guard_loc,
  2981→				LRK_MACRO_DEFINITION_LOCATION, NULL);
  2982→
  2983→  /* These are some funky cases we don't want to warn about.  */
  2984→  if (body_loc_exp == guard_loc_exp
  2985→      || next_loc_exp == guard_loc_exp
  2986→      || body_loc_exp == next_loc_exp)
  2987→    return;
  2988→
  2989→  /* Find the macro maps for the macro expansions.  */
  2990→  const line_map *body_map = linemap_lookup (line_table, body_loc);
  2991→  const line_map *next_map = linemap_lookup (line_table, next_loc);
  2992→  const line_map *guard_map = linemap_lookup (line_table, guard_loc);
  2993→
  2994→  /* Now see if the following token (after the body) is coming from the
  2995→     same macro expansion.  If it is, it might be a problem.  */
  2996→  if (body_map != next_map)
  2997→    return;
  2998→
  2999→  /* The conditional itself must not come from the same expansion, because
  3000→     we don't want to warn about
  3001→     #define IF if (x) x++; y++
  3002→     and similar.  */
  3003→  if (guard_map == body_map)
  3004→    return;
  3005→
  3006→  /* Handle the case where NEXT and BODY come from the same expansion while
  3007→     GUARD doesn't, yet we shouldn't warn.  E.g.
  3008→
  3009→       #define GUARD if (...)
  3010→       #define GUARD2 GUARD
  3011→
  3012→     and in the definition of another macro:
  3013→
  3014→       GUARD2
  3015→	foo ();
  3016→       return 1;
  3017→   */
  3018→  while (linemap_macro_expansion_map_p (guard_map))
  3019→    {
  3020→      const line_map_macro *mm = linemap_check_macro (guard_map);
  3021→      guard_loc_exp = mm->get_expansion_point_location ();
  3022→      guard_map = linemap_lookup (line_table, guard_loc_exp);
  3023→      if (guard_map == body_map)
  3024→	return;
  3025→    }
  3026→
  3027→  auto_diagnostic_group d;
  3028→  if (warning_at (body_loc, OPT_Wmultistatement_macros,
  3029→		  "macro expands to multiple statements"))
  3030→    inform (guard_loc, "some parts of macro expansion are not guarded by "
  3031→	    "this %qs clause", guard_tinfo_to_string (keyword));
  3032→}

  3034→/* Return struct or union type if the alignment of data member, FIELD,
  3035→   is less than the alignment of TYPE.  Otherwise, return NULL_TREE.
  3036→   If RVALUE is true, only arrays evaluate to pointers.  */
  3037→
  3038→static tree
  3039→check_alignment_of_packed_member (tree type, tree field, bool rvalue)
  3040→{
  3041→  /* Check alignment of the data member.  */
  3042→  if (TREE_CODE (field) == FIELD_DECL
  3043→      && (DECL_PACKED (field) || TYPE_PACKED (TREE_TYPE (field)))
  3044→      /* Ignore FIELDs not laid out yet.  */
  3045→      && DECL_FIELD_OFFSET (field)
  3046→      && (!rvalue || TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (field)) == ARRAY_TYPE))
  3047→    {
  3048→      /* Check the expected alignment against the field alignment.  */
  3049→      unsigned int type_align = min_align_of_type (type);
  3050→      tree context = DECL_CONTEXT (field);
  3051→      unsigned int record_align = min_align_of_type (context);
  3052→      if (record_align < type_align)
  3053→	return context;
  3054→      tree field_off = byte_position (field);
  3055→      if (!multiple_of_p (TREE_TYPE (field_off), field_off,
  3056→			  size_int (type_align)))
  3057→	return context;
  3058→    }
  3059→
  3060→  return NULL_TREE;
  3061→}
  3062→
  3063→/* Return struct or union type if the right hand value, RHS,
  3064→   is an address which takes the unaligned address of packed member
  3065→   of struct or union when assigning to TYPE.
  3066→   Otherwise, return NULL_TREE.  */
  3067→
  3068→static tree
  3069→check_address_of_packed_member (tree type, tree rhs)
  3070→{
  3071→  bool rvalue = true;
  3072→  bool indirect = false;
  3073→
  3074→  if (INDIRECT_REF_P (rhs))
  3075→    {
  3076→      rhs = TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 0);
  3077→      STRIP_NOPS (rhs);
  3078→      indirect = true;
  3079→    }
  3080→
  3081→  if (TREE_CODE (rhs) == ADDR_EXPR)
  3082→    {
  3083→      rhs = TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 0);
  3084→      rvalue = indirect;
  3085→    }
  3086→
  3087→  if (!POINTER_TYPE_P (type))
  3088→    return NULL_TREE;
  3089→
  3090→  type = TREE_TYPE (type);
  3091→
  3092→  tree context = NULL_TREE;
  3093→
  3094→  /* Check alignment of the object.  */
  3095→  while (handled_component_p (rhs))
  3096→    {
  3097→      if (TREE_CODE (rhs) == COMPONENT_REF)
  3098→	{
  3099→	  tree field = TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 1);
  3100→	  context = check_alignment_of_packed_member (type, field, rvalue);
  3101→	  if (context)
  3102→	    break;
  3103→	}
  3104→      if (TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (rhs)) == ARRAY_TYPE)
  3105→	rvalue = false;
  3106→      if (rvalue)
  3107→	return NULL_TREE;
  3108→      rhs = TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 0);
  3109→    }
  3110→
  3111→  return context;
  3112→}
  3113→
  3114→/* Check and warn if the right hand value, RHS,
  3115→   is an address which takes the unaligned address of packed member
  3116→   of struct or union when assigning to TYPE.  */
  3117→
  3118→static void
  3119→check_and_warn_address_of_packed_member (tree type, tree rhs)
  3120→{
  3121→  bool nop_p = false;
  3122→  tree orig_rhs;
  3123→
  3124→  do
  3125→    {
  3126→      while (TREE_CODE (rhs) == COMPOUND_EXPR)
  3127→	rhs = TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 1);
  3128→      orig_rhs = rhs;
  3129→      STRIP_NOPS (rhs);
  3130→      nop_p |= orig_rhs != rhs;
  3131→    }
  3132→  while (orig_rhs != rhs);
  3133→
  3134→  if (TREE_CODE (rhs) == COND_EXPR)
  3135→    {
  3136→      /* Check the THEN path.  */
  3137→      check_and_warn_address_of_packed_member
  3138→	(type, TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 1));
  3139→
  3140→      /* Check the ELSE path.  */
  3141→      check_and_warn_address_of_packed_member
  3142→	(type, TREE_OPERAND (rhs, 2));
  3143→    }
  3144→  else
  3145→    {
  3146→      if (nop_p)
  3147→	{
  3148→	  switch (TREE_CODE (rhs))
  3149→	    {
  3150→	    case ADDR_EXPR:
  3151→	      /* Address is taken.   */
  3152→	    case PARM_DECL:
  3153→	    case VAR_DECL:
  3154→	      /* Pointer conversion.  */
  3155→	      break;
  3156→	    case CALL_EXPR:
  3157→	      /* Function call. */
  3158→	      break;
  3159→	    default:
  3160→	      return;
  3161→	    }
  3162→	}
  3163→
  3164→      tree context
  3165→	= check_address_of_packed_member (type, rhs);
  3166→      if (context)
  3167→	{
  3168→	  location_t loc = EXPR_LOC_OR_LOC (rhs, input_location);
  3169→	  warning_at (loc, OPT_Waddress_of_packed_member,
  3170→		      "taking address of packed member of %qT may result "
  3171→		      "in an unaligned pointer value",
  3172→		      context);
  3173→	}
  3174→    }
  3175→}
  3176→
  3177→/* Warn if the right hand value, RHS,
  3178→   is an address which takes the unaligned address of packed member
  3179→   of struct or union when assigning to TYPE.  */
  3180→
  3181→void
  3182→warn_for_address_of_packed_member (tree type, tree rhs)
  3183→{
  3184→  if (!warn_address_of_packed_member)
  3185→    return;
  3186→
  3187→  /* Don't warn if we don't assign RHS to a pointer.  */
  3188→  if (!POINTER_TYPE_P (type))
  3189→    return;
  3190→
  3191→  check_and_warn_address_of_packed_member (type, rhs);
  3192→}

  3197→plus_one (tree expr)

  3203→/* Try to strip the expressions from around a VLA bound added internally
  3204→   to make it fit the domain mold, including any casts, and return
  3205→   the result.  The goal is to obtain the PARM_DECL the VLA bound may
  3206→   refer to.  */
  3207→
  3208→static tree
  3209→vla_bound_parm_decl (tree expr)
  3210→{
  3211→  if (!expr)
  3212→    return NULL_TREE;
  3213→
  3214→  if (TREE_CODE (expr) == NOP_EXPR)
  3215→    expr = TREE_OPERAND (expr, 0);
  3216→  if (TREE_CODE (expr) == PLUS_EXPR
  3217→      && integer_all_onesp (TREE_OPERAND (expr, 1)))
  3218→    {
  3219→      expr = TREE_OPERAND (expr, 0);
  3220→      if (TREE_CODE (expr) == NOP_EXPR)
  3221→	expr = TREE_OPERAND (expr, 0);
  3222→    }
  3223→  if (TREE_CODE (expr) == SAVE_EXPR)
  3224→    {
  3225→      expr = TREE_OPERAND (expr, 0);
  3226→      if (TREE_CODE (expr) == NOP_EXPR)
  3227→	expr = TREE_OPERAND (expr, 0);
  3228→    }
  3229→  return expr;
  3230→}

  3232→/* Diagnose mismatches in VLA bounds between function parameters NEWPARMS
  3233→   of pointer types on a redeclaration of a function previously declared
  3234→   with CURPARMS at ORIGLOC.  */
  3235→
  3236→static void
  3237→warn_parm_ptrarray_mismatch (location_t origloc, tree curparms, tree newparms)
  3238→{
  3239→  /* Maps each named integral parameter seen so far to its position
  3240→     in the argument list; used to associate VLA sizes with arguments.  */
  3241→  hash_map<tree, unsigned> curparm2pos;
  3242→  hash_map<tree, unsigned> newparm2pos;
  3243→
  3244→  unsigned parmpos = 1;
  3245→  for (tree curp = curparms, newp = newparms; curp && newp;
  3246→       curp = TREE_CHAIN (curp), newp = TREE_CHAIN (newp), ++parmpos)
  3247→    {
  3248→      tree curtyp = TREE_TYPE (curp), newtyp = TREE_TYPE (newp);
  3249→      if (INTEGRAL_TYPE_P (curtyp))
  3250→	{
  3251→	  /* Only add named parameters; unnamed ones cannot be referred
  3252→	     to in VLA bounds.  */
  3253→	  if (DECL_NAME (curp))
  3254→	    curparm2pos.put (curp, parmpos);
  3255→	  if (DECL_NAME (newp))
  3256→	    newparm2pos.put (newp, parmpos);
  3257→
  3258→	  continue;
  3259→	}
  3260→
  3261→      /* The parameter types should match at this point so only test one.  */
  3262→      if (TREE_CODE (curtyp) != POINTER_TYPE)
  3263→	continue;
  3264→
  3265→      do
  3266→	{
  3267→	  curtyp = TREE_TYPE (curtyp);
  3268→	  newtyp = TREE_TYPE (newtyp);
  3269→
  3270→	  if (!newtyp)
  3271→	    /* Bail on error.  */
  3272→	    return;
  3273→	}
  3274→      while (TREE_CODE (curtyp) == POINTER_TYPE
  3275→	     && TREE_CODE (newtyp) == POINTER_TYPE);
  3276→
  3277→      if (TREE_CODE (curtyp) != ARRAY_TYPE
  3278→	  || TREE_CODE (newtyp) != ARRAY_TYPE)
  3279→	{
  3280→	  if (curtyp == error_mark_node
  3281→	      || newtyp == error_mark_node)
  3282→	    /* Bail on error.  */
  3283→	    return;
  3284→
  3285→	  continue;
  3286→	}
  3287→
  3288→      tree curdom = TYPE_DOMAIN (curtyp), newdom = TYPE_DOMAIN (newtyp);
  3289→      tree curbnd = curdom ? TYPE_MAX_VALUE (curdom) : NULL_TREE;
  3290→      tree newbnd = newdom ? TYPE_MAX_VALUE (newdom) : NULL_TREE;
  3291→
  3292→      if (DECL_P (curp))
  3293→	origloc = DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (curp);
  3294→      else if (EXPR_P (curp) && EXPR_HAS_LOCATION (curp))
  3295→	origloc = EXPR_LOCATION (curp);
  3296→
  3297→      /* The location of the parameter in the current redeclaration.  */
  3298→      location_t newloc = DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (newp);
  3299→      if (origloc == UNKNOWN_LOCATION)
  3300→	origloc = newloc;
  3301→
  3302→      /* Issue -Warray-parameter unless one or more mismatches involves
  3303→	 a VLA bound; then issue -Wvla-parameter.  */
  3304→      int opt = OPT_Warray_parameter_;
  3305→      /* Traverse the two array types looking for variable bounds and
  3306→	 comparing the two in each pair for mismatches either in their
  3307→	 positions in the function parameter list or lexicographically
  3308→	 for others.  Record the 1-based parameter position of each
  3309→	 mismatch in BNDVEC, and the location of each parameter in
  3310→	 the mismatch in WARNLOC (for the new parameter list) and
  3311→	 NOTELOC (for the current parameter list).  */
  3312→      unsigned bndpos = 1;
  3313→      auto_vec<int> bndvec;
  3314→      gcc_rich_location warnloc (newloc);
  3315→      gcc_rich_location noteloc (origloc);
  3316→      for ( ; curtyp || newtyp;
  3317→	    ++bndpos,
  3318→	      curbnd = curdom ? TYPE_MAX_VALUE (curdom) : NULL_TREE,
  3319→	      newbnd = newdom ? TYPE_MAX_VALUE (newdom) : NULL_TREE)
  3320→	{
  3321→	  /* Try to strip each bound down to the PARM_DECL if it does
  3322→	     correspond to one.  Either bound can be null if it's
  3323→	     unspecified (i.e., has the [*] form).  */
  3324→	  curbnd = vla_bound_parm_decl (curbnd);
  3325→	  newbnd = vla_bound_parm_decl (newbnd);
  3326→
  3327→	  /* Peel the current bound off CURTYP and NEWTYP, skipping
  3328→	     over any subsequent pointer types.  */
  3329→	  if (curtyp && TREE_CODE (curtyp) == ARRAY_TYPE)
  3330→	    {
  3331→	      do
  3332→		curtyp = TREE_TYPE (curtyp);
  3333→	      while (TREE_CODE (curtyp) == POINTER_TYPE);
  3334→	      if (TREE_CODE (curtyp) == ARRAY_TYPE)
  3335→		curdom = TYPE_DOMAIN (curtyp);
  3336→	      else
  3337→		curdom = NULL_TREE;
  3338→	    }
  3339→	  else
  3340→	    curtyp = NULL_TREE;
  3341→
  3342→	  if (newtyp && TREE_CODE (newtyp) == ARRAY_TYPE)
  3343→	    {
  3344→	      do
  3345→		newtyp = TREE_TYPE (newtyp);
  3346→	      while (TREE_CODE (newtyp) == POINTER_TYPE);
  3347→	      if (TREE_CODE (newtyp) == ARRAY_TYPE)
  3348→		newdom = TYPE_DOMAIN (newtyp);
  3349→	      else
  3350→		newdom = NULL_TREE;
  3351→	    }
  3352→	  else
  3353→	    newtyp = NULL_TREE;
  3354→
  3355→	  /* Move on to the next bound if this one is unspecified.  */
  3356→	  if (!curbnd && !newbnd)
  3357→	    continue;
  3358→
  3359→	  /* Try to find each bound in the parameter list.  */
  3360→	  const unsigned* const pcurbndpos = curparm2pos.get (curbnd);
  3361→	  const unsigned* const pnewbndpos = newparm2pos.get (newbnd);
  3362→	  /* Move on if both bounds refer to the same parameter.  */
  3363→	  if (pcurbndpos && pnewbndpos && *pcurbndpos == *pnewbndpos)
  3364→	    continue;
  3365→
  3366→	  /* Move on if the bounds look the same.  */
  3367→	  if (!pcurbndpos && !pnewbndpos
  3368→	      && curbnd && newbnd
  3369→	      && operand_equal_p (curbnd, newbnd,
  3370→				  OEP_DECL_NAME | OEP_LEXICOGRAPHIC))
  3371→	    continue;
  3372→
  3373→	  if ((curbnd && TREE_CODE (curbnd) != INTEGER_CST)
  3374→	      || (newbnd && TREE_CODE (newbnd) != INTEGER_CST))
  3375→	    opt = OPT_Wvla_parameter;
  3376→
  3377→	  /* Record the mismatch.  */
  3378→	  bndvec.safe_push (bndpos);
  3379→	  /* Underline the bounding parameter in the declaration.  */
  3380→	  if (curbnd && TREE_CODE (curbnd) == PARM_DECL)
  3381→	    noteloc.add_range (DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (curbnd));
  3382→	  if (newbnd && TREE_CODE (newbnd) == PARM_DECL)
  3383→	    warnloc.add_range (DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (newbnd));
  3384→	}
  3385→
  3386→      const unsigned nbnds = bndvec.length ();
  3387→      if (!nbnds)
  3388→	continue;
  3389→
  3390→      /* Use attr_access to format the parameter types.  */
  3391→      attr_access spec = { };
  3392→      const std::string newparmstr = spec.array_as_string (TREE_TYPE (newp));
  3393→      const std::string curparmstr = spec.array_as_string (TREE_TYPE (curp));
  3394→
  3395→      if (warning_n (&warnloc, opt, nbnds,
  3396→		     "mismatch in bound %Z of argument %u declared as %s",
  3397→		     "mismatch in bounds %Z of argument %u declared as %s",
  3398→		     bndvec.address (), nbnds, parmpos, newparmstr.c_str ()))
  3399→	inform (&noteloc, "previously declared as %s",	curparmstr.c_str ());
  3400→    }
  3401→}

  3403→/* Format EXPR if nonnull and return the formatted string.  If EXPR is

  3415→
  3416→/* Detect and diagnose a mismatch between an attribute access specification
  3417→   on the original declaration of FNDECL and that on the parameters NEWPARMS
  3418→   from its redeclaration.  ORIGLOC is the location of the first declaration
  3419→   (FNDECL's is set to the location of the redeclaration).  */
  3420→
  3421→void
  3422→warn_parm_array_mismatch (location_t origloc, tree fndecl, tree newparms)
  3423→{
  3424→  /* The original parameter list (copied from the original declaration
  3425→     into the current [re]declaration, FNDECL)).  The two are equal if
  3426→     and only if FNDECL is the first declaration.  */
  3427→  tree curparms = DECL_ARGUMENTS (fndecl);
  3428→  if (!curparms || !newparms || curparms == newparms)
  3429→    return;
  3430→
  3431→  if (TREE_CODE (curparms) != PARM_DECL
  3432→      || TREE_CODE (newparms) != PARM_DECL)
  3433→    return;
  3434→  /* Extract the (possibly empty) attribute access specification from
  3435→     the declaration and its type (it doesn't yet reflect those created
  3436→     in response to NEWPARMS).  */
  3437→  rdwr_map cur_idx;
  3438→  tree fntype = TREE_TYPE (fndecl);
  3439→  init_attr_rdwr_indices (&cur_idx, TYPE_ATTRIBUTES (fntype));
  3440→
  3441→  /* Build a (possibly null) chain of access attributes corresponding
  3442→     to NEWPARMS.  */
  3443→  const bool builtin = fndecl_built_in_p (fndecl);
  3444→  tree newattrs = build_attr_access_from_parms (newparms, builtin);
  3445→
  3446→  /* Extract the (possibly empty) attribute access specification from
  3447→     NEWATTRS.  */
  3448→  rdwr_map new_idx;
  3449→  init_attr_rdwr_indices (&new_idx, newattrs);
  3450→
  3451→  if (cur_idx.is_empty () && new_idx.is_empty ())
  3452→    {
  3453→      /* If both specs are empty check pointers to VLAs for mismatches. */
  3454→      warn_parm_ptrarray_mismatch (origloc, curparms, newparms);
  3455→      return;
  3456→    }
  3457→  /* ...otherwise, if at least one spec isn't empty there may be mismatches,
  3458→     such as between f(T*) and f(T[1]), where the former mapping would be
  3459→     empty.  */
  3460→
  3461→  /* Create an empty access specification and use it for pointers with
  3462→     no spec of their own.  */
  3463→  attr_access ptr_spec = { };
  3464→
  3465→  /* Iterate over the two lists of function parameters, comparing their
  3466→     respective mappings and diagnosing mismatches.  */
  3467→  unsigned parmpos = 0;
  3468→  for (tree curp = curparms, newp = newparms; curp;
  3469→       curp = TREE_CHAIN (curp), newp = TREE_CHAIN (newp), ++parmpos)
  3470→    {
  3471→      if (!newp)
  3472→	/* Bail on invalid redeclarations with fewer arguments.  */
  3473→	return;
  3474→
  3475→      /* Only check pointers and C++ references.  */
  3476→      tree curptype = TREE_TYPE (curp);
  3477→      tree newptype = TREE_TYPE (newp);
  3478→      if (!POINTER_TYPE_P (curptype) || !POINTER_TYPE_P (newptype))
  3479→	continue;
  3480→
  3481→      /* Skip mismatches in __builtin_va_list that is commonly
  3482→	 an array but that in declarations of built-ins decays
  3483→	 to a pointer.  */
  3484→      if (builtin && TREE_TYPE (newptype) == TREE_TYPE (va_list_type_node))
  3485→	continue;
  3486→
  3487→      /* Access specs for the argument on the current (previous) and
  3488→	 new (to replace the current) declarations.  Either may be null,
  3489→	 indicating the parameter is an ordinary pointer with no size
  3490→	 associated with it.  */
  3491→      attr_access *cura = cur_idx.get (parmpos);
  3492→      attr_access *newa = new_idx.get (parmpos);
  3493→
  3494→      if (!newa)
  3495→	{
  3496→	  /* Continue of both parameters are pointers with no size
  3497→	     associated with it.  */
  3498→	  if (!cura)
  3499→	    continue;
  3500→
  3501→	  /* Otherwise point at PTR_SPEC and set its parameter pointer
  3502→	     and number.  */
  3503→	  newa = &ptr_spec;
  3504→	  newa->ptr = newp;
  3505→	  newa->ptrarg = parmpos;
  3506→	}
  3507→      else if (!cura)
  3508→	{
  3509→	  cura = &ptr_spec;
  3510→	  cura->ptr = curp;
  3511→	  cura->ptrarg = parmpos;
  3512→	}
  3513→
  3514→      /* Set if the parameter is [re]declared as a VLA.  */
  3515→      const bool cur_vla_p = cura->size || cura->minsize == HOST_WIDE_INT_M1U;
  3516→      const bool new_vla_p = newa->size || newa->minsize == HOST_WIDE_INT_M1U;
  3517→
  3518→      if (DECL_P (curp))
  3519→	origloc = DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (curp);
  3520→      else if (EXPR_P (curp) && EXPR_HAS_LOCATION (curp))
  3521→	origloc = EXPR_LOCATION (curp);
  3522→
  3523→      /* The location of the parameter in the current redeclaration.  */
  3524→      location_t newloc = DECL_SOURCE_LOCATION (newp);
  3525→      if (origloc == UNKNOWN_LOCATION)
  3526→	origloc = newloc;
  3527→
  3528→      const std::string newparmstr = newa->array_as_string (newptype);
  3529→      const std::string curparmstr = cura->array_as_string (curptype);
  3530→      if (new_vla_p && !cur_vla_p)
  3531→	{
  3532→	  if (warning_at (newloc, OPT_Wvla_parameter,
  3533→			  "argument %u of type %s declared as "
  3534→			  "a variable length array",
  3535→			  parmpos + 1, newparmstr.c_str ()))
  3536→	    inform (origloc,
  3537→		    (cura == &ptr_spec
  3538→		     ? G_("previously declared as a pointer %s")
  3539→		     : G_("previously declared as an ordinary array %s")),
  3540→		    curparmstr.c_str ());
  3541→	  continue;
  3542→	}
  3543→
  3544→      if (newa == &ptr_spec)
  3545→	{
  3546→	  /* The new declaration uses the pointer form.  Detect mismatches
  3547→	     between the pointer and a previous array or VLA forms.  */
  3548→	  if (cura->minsize == HOST_WIDE_INT_M1U)
  3549→	    {
  3550→	      /* Diagnose a pointer/VLA mismatch.  */
  3551→	      if (warning_at (newloc, OPT_Wvla_parameter,
  3552→			      "argument %u of type %s declared "
  3553→			      "as a pointer",
  3554→			      parmpos + 1, newparmstr.c_str ()))
  3555→		inform (origloc,
  3556→			"previously declared as a variable length array %s",
  3557→			curparmstr.c_str ());
  3558→	      continue;
  3559→	    }
  3560→
  3561→	  if (cura->minsize && cura->minsize != HOST_WIDE_INT_M1U)
  3562→	    {
  3563→	      /* Diagnose mismatches between arrays with a constant
  3564→		 bound and pointers.  */
  3565→	      if (warning_at (newloc, OPT_Warray_parameter_,
  3566→			      "argument %u of type %s declared "
  3567→			      "as a pointer",
  3568→			      parmpos + 1, newparmstr.c_str ()))
  3569→		inform (origloc, "previously declared as an array %s",
  3570→			curparmstr.c_str ());
  3571→	      continue;
  3572→	    }
  3573→	}
  3574→
  3575→      if (!new_vla_p && cur_vla_p)
  3576→	{
  3577→	  if (warning_at (newloc, OPT_Wvla_parameter,
  3578→			  "argument %u of type %s declared "
  3579→			  "as an ordinary array",
  3580→			  parmpos + 1, newparmstr.c_str ()))
  3581→	    inform (origloc,
  3582→		    "previously declared as a variable length array %s",
  3583→		    curparmstr.c_str ());
  3584→	  continue;
  3585→	}
  3586→
  3587→      /* Move on to the next pair of parameters if both of the current
  3588→	 pair are VLAs with a single variable bound that refers to
  3589→	 a parameter at the same position.  */
  3590→      if (newa->size && cura->size
  3591→	  && newa->sizarg != UINT_MAX
  3592→	  && newa->sizarg == cura->sizarg
  3593→	  && newa->minsize == cura->minsize
  3594→	  && !TREE_PURPOSE (newa->size) && !TREE_PURPOSE (cura->size))
  3595→	continue;
  3596→
  3597→      if (newa->size || cura->size)
  3598→	{
  3599→	  unsigned newunspec, curunspec;
  3600→	  unsigned newbnds = newa->vla_bounds (&newunspec) + newunspec;
  3601→	  unsigned curbnds = cura->vla_bounds (&curunspec) + curunspec;
  3602→
  3603→	  if (newbnds != curbnds)
  3604→	    {
  3605→	      if (warning_n (newloc, OPT_Wvla_parameter, newbnds,
  3606→			     "argument %u of type %s declared with "
  3607→			     "%u variable bound",
  3608→			     "argument %u of type %s declared with "
  3609→			     "%u variable bounds",
  3610→			     parmpos + 1, newparmstr.c_str (),
  3611→			     newbnds))
  3612→		inform_n (origloc, curbnds,
  3613→			  "previously declared as %s with %u variable bound",
  3614→			  "previously declared as %s with %u variable bounds",
  3615→			  curparmstr.c_str (), curbnds);
  3616→	      continue;
  3617→	    }
  3618→
  3619→	  if (newunspec > curunspec)

Author: Marek Polacek <polacek@redhat.com>

    c++: #pragma doesn't disable -Wunused-label [PR113582]
    
    The PR complains that
    
      void do_something(){
        #pragma GCC diagnostic push
        #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wunused-label"
        start:;
        #pragma GCC diagnostic pop
      } #1
    
    doesn't work.  That's because we warn_for_unused_label only while we're
    in finish_function, meaning we're at #1 where we're outside the #pragma
    region.  We can use suppress_warning + warning_suppressed_p to fix this.
    
    Note that I'm not using TREE_USED.  Propagating it in tsubst_stmt/LABEL_EXPR
    from decl to label would mean that we don't warn in do_something2, but
    I think we want the warning there: we're in a template and the goto is
    a discarded statement.

messages.content:
## Summary

I've successfully implemented the fix for the issue where `#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wunused-label"` was not being respected for unused labels in template functions with `if constexpr`.

### Changes Made

**1. gcc/c-family/c-warn.cc (warn_for_unused_label function at line 2188)**
   - Added a check for `warning_suppressed_p(label, OPT_Wunused_label)` before emitting the warning
   - This ensures labels with suppressed warnings don't trigger the unused-label warning

**2. gcc/cp/parser.cc (cp_parser_label_for_labeled_statement at line 13113)**
   - When creating a label, check if `-Wunused-label` is enabled at `input_location`
   - If not enabled (e.g., due to `#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored`), suppress the warning for that label
   - This captures the pragma diagnostic state at the exact location where the label is defined

**3. gcc/cp/pt.cc (tsubst_stmt LABEL_EXPR case at line 18844)**
   - When instantiating template labels, use `copy_warning` to copy the warning suppression state from the template label to the instantiated label
   - This ensures the pragma diagnostic state is preserved during template instantiation

### How It Works

The fix addresses the root cause: warnings for unused labels were being checked after the function finished, which was outside the `#pragma GCC diagnostic` region. The solution:

1. **Capture pragma state**: When a label is parsed, check if `-Wunused-label` is enabled at that location and mark the label accordingly
2. **Respect suppression**: When checking for unused labels, verify if warnings have been suppressed for that specific label
3. **Preserve state in templates**: During template instantiation, copy the warning suppression state so labels in template instantiations retain the pragma diagnostic context from the original template definition

This ensures that the pragma directives are respected while still warning about genuinely unused labels when appropriate.

But `\def` is not just a regular macro expansion - it's a macro that has SIDE EFFECTS (it modifies the namespace).

The issue is that when `expandOnce()` is called on `\def`, the `def` function in macros.js is invoked, and it calls `context.macros.set()` immediately.

So the problem is that macro expansion with side effects happens during token consumption, which happens before we're ready.

I think the real fix is different. Instead of trying to delay the expansion, we need to ensure that when the environment's arguments are parsed, we don't consume tokens beyond what's needed.

   - This should add `\x=1` to the undo stack (the old value)

messages.content:
## Summary

I've successfully fixed the array cell scoping issue (#1989) in KaTeX. Here's what was done:

### The Problem
When parsing array environments like `\begin{matrix}...\end{matrix}`, macro definitions (e.g., `\def\x{2}`) at the start of a cell were being executed during token lookahead, **before** the cell's scoping group was created. This caused the macro definitions to leak to other cells and outside the array environment.

For example:
- `\def\x{1}\begin{matrix}\def\x{2}&\x\end{matrix}` was incorrectly rendering as `22` instead of the expected behavior where the second cell shows `1`.

### The Solution
The fix involved tracking macro state before and after token lookahead to properly scope macros to their cells:

1. **Modified `/workspace/KaTeX/src/Parser.js`** (lines 436-450, 462-469):
   - Added code to save macro state before parsing function arguments
   - Passed this state (`preLookaheadMacros`) to function handlers via the context

2. **Modified `/workspace/KaTeX/src/functions/environment.js`** (line 17):
   - Updated the handler to receive `preLookaheadMacros` from context
   - Passed it to environment handlers

3. **Modified `/workspace/KaTeX/src/environments/array.js`** (lines 53-71, 89-108):
   - Added `preLookaheadMacros` parameter to `parseArray` function
   - After creating the first cell group, compared current macro state with pre-lookahead state
   - Registered any macros that were added or modified during lookahead in the cell's undo stack
   - This ensures they get properly restored/removed when the cell group ends

4. **Modified type definitions** in `/workspace/KaTeX/src/defineFunction.js` (line 19) and `/workspace/KaTeX/src/defineEnvironment.js` (line 20):
   - Added `preLookaheadMacros?: {[string]: any}` to `FunctionContext` and `EnvContext` types

### Testing
- All 960 tests pass, including the previously failing "array cells generate groups" test
- The fix properly scopes macro definitions to their cells, preventing leakage

### Files Modified
1. `/workspace/KaTeX/src/Parser.js`
2. `/workspace/KaTeX/src/functions/environment.js`
3. `/workspace/KaTeX/src/environments/array.js`
4. `/workspace/KaTeX/src/defineFunction.js`
5. `/workspace/KaTeX/src/defineEnvironment.js`

# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive/irreversible git commands (like push --force, hard reset, etc) unless the user explicitly requests them 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- Avoid git commit --amend.  ONLY use --amend when either (1) user explicitly requested amend OR (2) adding edits from pre-commit hook (additional instructions below) 
- Before amending: ALWAYS check authorship (git log -1 --format='%an %ae')

1. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:

  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).

  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"

3. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. run the following commands in parallel:

   - Run git status to make sure the commit succeeded.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry ONCE. If it succeeds but files were modified by the hook, verify it's safe to amend:
   - Check authorship: git log -1 --format='%an %ae'
   - Check not pushed: git status shows "Your branch is ahead"

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output-mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

b.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

_A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

c.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

Headlimit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). When unspecified, shows all results from ripgrep.

Skip using this tool when:
1. There is only a single, straightforward task
2. The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
3. The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
4. The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

Let's start by implementing memoization for the expensive calculations in your ProductList component.</assistant>

This will output the text "Hello World" to the console when executed.</assistant>

1. **Task States**: Use these states to track progress:

messages.content:
I found the issue! Looking at the code on lines 411-418, I can see that when the setter is called within a write-only atom's `write` function:

1. If `a === atom` (same atom), it calls `setAtomValue` and `invalidateDependents` 
2. If `a !== atom` (different atom), it calls `writeAtomState` recursively

The problem is that when async operations are happening in write-only atoms, the `set` calls for other atoms (line 416: `writeAtomState(state, a, v)`) don't include the `flushPending(state)` call that would notify subscribers.

However, looking more carefully at `writeAtomState`, I see that when it's called recursively for other atoms, if there are pending promises, the `flushPending` is only called when the promise resolves. But in our case, the async operations in the user's code are not returning promises from the `write` function—they're doing async work inside but not returning the promise.

Let me look at how `setAtomValue` and `invalidateDependents` work:

messages.content:
Perfect! I have successfully implemented a fix for the GitHub issue. Let me summarize what I accomplished:

## Summary

**Problem**: In Jotai v0.15.3, when using write-only atoms with async operations that call `set()` for other atoms, the components were not re-rendering even though the atom values were being updated correctly.

**Root Cause**: The issue was in the `writeAtomState` function in `src/core/vanilla.ts`. When async operations inside write-only atoms called `set()` for other atoms, those updates were committed to the state (via `commitAtomState`) but `flushPending()` was not called to notify subscribers, leaving components in a stale state.

**Solution**: I modified the setter function in `writeAtomState` (lines 411-423) to add a check after each `set()` operation. If there are pending atoms to be flushed (`state.p.size > 0`), it schedules a `flushPending(state)` call on the next tick using `Promise.resolve().then()`.

**The Fix** (`src/core/vanilla.ts:418-422`):
```typescript
// Ensure pending atoms are flushed after synchronous writes
// This handles the case where async operations call set() but don't return a promise
if (state.p.size > 0) {
  Promise.resolve().then(() => flushPending(state))
}
```

**Testing**:
1. ✅ Successfully reproduced the original issue with a test case
2. ✅ Confirmed the fix resolves the issue - components now re-render correctly
3. ✅ All existing tests pass (125 tests, 27 test suites) - no regressions
4. ✅ The fix handles the exact pattern from the user's issue

**Key Benefits**:
- **Minimal change**: Only 5 lines of code added
- **Backward compatible**: No breaking changes to existing functionality  
- **Targeted fix**: Specifically addresses async `set()` calls in write-only atoms
- **Performance conscious**: Only schedules flush when there are actually pending atoms

The fix ensures that when async operations in write-only atoms update other atoms using `set()`, the component subscribers are properly notified and re-render with the updated values.

Please check the content of the following 3 files at once and analyze the code content:
1) /workspace/jotai/tests/reproduce_issue.test.tsx
2) /workspace/jotai/src/core/vanilla.ts
3) /workspace/jotai/tests/edge_cases.test.tsx

It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool
Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

1. Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
2. Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
3. User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
4. User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
5. After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as todos
6. When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work. Ideally you should only have one todo as in_progress at a time
7. After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
1. There is only a single, straightforward task
2. The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
3. The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps

function.description: Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously. Available agent types and the tools they have access to: - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *) - statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit) - output-style-setup: Use this agent to create a Claude Code output style. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep) When using the Task tool, you must specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. When NOT to use the Agent tool: - If you want to read a specific file path, use the Read or Glob tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly - If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the Glob tool instead, to find the match more quickly - If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the Read tool instead of the Agent tool, to find the match more quickly - Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above Usage notes: 1. Launch multiple agents concurrently whenever possible, to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses 2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result. 3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you. 4. The agent's outputs should generally be trusted 5. Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since it is not aware of the user's intent 6. If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first. Use your judgement. 7. If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Task tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a code-reviewer agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls. Example usage: "code-reviewer": use this agent after you are done writing a signficant piece of code "greeting-responder": use this agent when to respond to user greetings with a friendly joke user: "Please write a function that checks if a number is prime" assistant: Sure let me write a function that checks if a number is prime assistant: First let me use the Write tool to write a function that checks if a number is prime assistant: I'm going to use the Write tool to write the following code: function isPrime(n) { if (n <= 1) return false for (let i = 2; i * i <= n; i++) { if (n % i === 0) return false } return true } Since a signficant piece of code was written and the task was completed, now use the code-reviewer agent to review the code assistant: Now let me use the code-reviewer agent to review the code assistant: Uses the Task tool to launch the with the code-reviewer agent user: "Hello" Since the user is greeting, use the greeting-responder agent to respond with a friendly joke assistant: "I'm going to use the Task tool to launch the with the greeting-responder agent"

function.description:
This is a tool for making multiple edits to a single file in one operation. It is built on top of the Edit tool and allows you to perform multiple find-and-replace operations efficiently. Prefer this tool over the Edit tool when you need to make multiple edits to the same file.

Before using this tool:

   - old_string: The text to replace (must match the file contents exactly, including all whitespace and indentation)
   - new_string: The edited text to replace the old_string
   - replace_all: Replace all occurences of old_string. This parameter is optional and defaults to false.

IMPORTANT:
- All edits are applied in sequence, in the order they are provided
- Each edit operates on the result of the previous edit
- All edits must be valid for the operation to succeed - if any edit fails, none will be applied
- This tool is ideal when you need to make several changes to different parts of the same file
- For Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files), use the NotebookEdit instead

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
1. All edits follow the same requirements as the single Edit tool
2. The edits are atomic - either all succeed or none are applied
3. Plan your edits carefully to avoid conflicts between sequential operations

WARNING:
- The tool will fail if edits.old_string doesn't match the file contents exactly (including whitespace)
- The tool will fail if edits.old_string and edits.new_string are the same
- Since edits are applied in sequence, ensure that earlier edits don't affect the text that later edits are trying to find

When making edits:
- Ensure all edits result in idiomatic, correct code
- Do not leave the code in a broken state
- Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- Use replace_all for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

If you want to create a new file, use:
- A new file path, including dir name if needed
- First edit: empty old_string and the new file's contents as new_string
- Subsequent edits: normal edit operations on the created content

function.name: Bash
function.description:
Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location
   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use `ls foo` to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
   - Examples of proper quoting:
     - cd "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)
     - cd /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail)
     - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct)
     - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail)
   - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command.
   - Capture the output of the command.

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background, which allows you to continue working while the command runs. You can monitor the output using the Bash tool as it becomes available. Never use `run_in_background` to run 'sleep' as it will return immediately. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
  - VERY IMPORTANT: You MUST avoid using search commands like `find` and `grep`. Instead use Grep, Glob, or Task to search. You MUST avoid read tools like `cat`, `head`, and `tail`, and use Read to read files.
 - If you _still_ need to run `grep`, STOP. ALWAYS USE ripgrep at `rg` first, which all Claude Code users have pre-installed.
  - When issuing multiple commands, use the ';' or '&&' operator to separate them. DO NOT use newlines (newlines are ok in quoted strings).
  - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it.
    <good-example>
    pytest /foo/bar/tests
    </good-example>
    <bad-example>
    cd /foo/bar && pytest tests
    </bad-example>

# Committing changes with git

When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

1. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Check for any sensitive information that shouldn't be committed
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message ending with:
   🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

   Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
   - Run git status to make sure the commit succeeded.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.

Important notes:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Task tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.

   🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

   Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request summary
3. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested, batch your tool calls together for optimal performance. ALWAYS run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- NEVER update the git config
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Task tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

function.name: GREP
function.description:
A powerful search tool built on ripgrep

  Usage:
  - ALWAYS use Grep for search tasks. NEVER invoke `grep` or `rg` as a Bash command. The Grep tool has been optimized for correct permissions and access.
  - Supports full regex syntax (e.g., "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+")

  - Use Task tool for open-ended searches requiring multiple rounds
  - Pattern syntax: Uses ripgrep (not grep) - literal braces need escaping (use `interface\{\}` to find `interface{}` in Go code)
  - Multiline matching: By default patterns match within single lines only. For cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`, use `multiline: true`

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

Outputmode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

_A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

headlimit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). When unspecified, shows all results from ripgrep.

MULTILINE.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Excellent! The implementation is complete and working. Let me summarize what I've implemented:

## Summary of Changes

I successfully implemented the fix for the issue where the operator cannot reconcile StatefulSets when `volumeClaimTemplates` are changed. The changes include:

### 1. Added VolumeClaimTemplates Change Detection (`pkg/collector/reconcile/statefulset.go:85-93`)

Added a check similar to the existing selector check that detects when `VolumeClaimTemplates` differ between the desired and existing StatefulSet. When a change is detected, the existing StatefulSet is deleted and will be recreated in the next reconcile cycle.

```go
// VolumeClaimTemplates is an immutable field, if set, we cannot modify it otherwise we will face reconciliation error.
if !apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(desired.Spec.VolumeClaimTemplates, existing.Spec.VolumeClaimTemplates) {
    params.Log.V(2).Info("Spec.VolumeClaimTemplates change detected, trying to delete, the new collector statefulset will be created in the next reconcile cycle", "statefulset.name", existing.Name, "statefulset.namespace", existing.Namespace)

    if err := params.Client.Delete(ctx, existing); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete statefulset: %w", err)
    }
    continue
}
```

### 2. Cleaned Up VolumeClaimTemplates Function Signature

- Removed the unused `config.Config` parameter from `VolumeClaimTemplates` function (`pkg/collector/volumeclaim.go:27`)
- Removed the unused import for `internal/config` package
- Updated the call to `VolumeClaimTemplates` in `statefulset.go` to match the new signature

This fix ensures that:

1. **Immutable Field Handling**: The operator now properly handles changes to the immutable `VolumeClaimTemplates` field by deleting and recreating the StatefulSet, similar to how selector changes are handled.

2. **No Reconciliation Failures**: Users will no longer encounter the "StatefulSet.apps is invalid: spec: Forbidden" error when `volumeClaimTemplates` are changed.

3. **Consistent Behavior**: The implementation follows the same pattern used for other immutable fields like `Selector`, ensuring consistency in the codebase.

The solution is minimal and follows the existing patterns in the codebase, making it a safe and maintainable fix for the reported issue.

function.description:
A powerful search tool built on ripgrep

  Usage:
  - ALWAYS use Grep for search tasks. NEVER invoke `grep` or `rg` as a Bash command. The Grep tool has been optimized for correct permissions and access.
  - Supports full regex syntax (e.g., "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+")
  - Filter files with glob parameter (e.g., "*.js", "**/*.tsx") or type parameter (e.g., "js", "py", "rust")
  - Output modes: "content" shows matching lines, "files_with_matches" shows only file paths (default), "count" shows match counts
  - Use Task tool for open-ended searches requiring multiple rounds
  - Pattern syntax: Uses ripgrep (not grep) - literal braces need escaping (use `interface\{\}` to find `interface{}` in Go code)
  - Multiline matching: By default patterns match within single lines only. For cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`, use `multiline: true`

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

Glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

OUTPUTMode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

_c.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

HEADLIMIT.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). When unspecified, shows all results from ripgrep.

Multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The command to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/testbed/file.py` or `/testbed`.

file_text.description: Required for the `create` command, contains the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required for the `str_replace` command, specifies the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional for the `str_replace` command to specify the replacement string. Required for the `insert` command to specify the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required for the `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line specified.

view_range.description: Optional for the `view` command when `path` points to a file. Specifies the line range to view. E.g., [11, 12] shows lines 11 and 12. Indexing starts at 1. Use [start_line, -1] to show all lines from `start_line` to the end.

concise.description: Optional for the `view` command. If `True`, displays a concise skeletal view of the file. Very useful for localization tasks. Highly recommended for large files.

Description: Search for a term in either a directory or a single file.

Behavior:
* If `--path` points to a directory (default is `.`), we recursively search all non-hidden files and directories.
* If `--path` points to a file, we run `grep -n` on that file to find line numbers containing the search term.
* If more than 100 files match (directory search scenario), the tool will stop listing and inform you to narrow your search.
* If no files are found that match your search term, the tool will inform you of that as well.

**Parameters:**
  1. **search_term** (`string`, required): The term to search for in files.
  2. **path** (`string`, optional): The file or directory in which to search. If not provided, defaults to the current directory (i.e., `.`).

`io.fits.FITSDiff` only reports differences in files if they exist. Comparing a file to itself should never yield a difference.

```python
from astropy.io import fits
col = fits.Column('a', format='QD', array=[[0], [0, 0]])

hdu.writeto('diffbug.fits', overwrite=True)

print(fits.FITSDiff('diffbug.fits', 'diffbug.fits').identical)
fits.printdiff('diffbug.fits', 'diffbug.fits')

```

from astropy.io import fits

    col1 = fits.Column('empty_vla', format='QD', array=[[], []])

    print(f"  Identical: {diff.identical}")
    assert diff.identical, "Empty VLA arrays should be identical"
    
    if os.path.exists('test_empty_vla.fits'):

    col2 = fits.Column('single_vla', format='QD', array=[[5], [6, 7]])
    hdu2 = fits.BinTableHDU.from_columns([col2])
    hdu2.writeto('test_single_vla.fits', overwrite=True)
    
    diff = fits.FITSDiff('test_single_vla.fits', 'test_single_vla.fits')

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The command to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/testbed/file.py` or `/testbed`.

file_text.description: Required for the `create` command, contains the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required for the `str_replace` command, specifies the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional for the `str_replace` command to specify the replacement string. Required for the `insert` command to specify the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required for the `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line specified.

view_range.description: Optional for the `view` command when `path` points to a file. Specifies the line range to view. E.g., [11, 12] shows lines 11 and 12. Indexing starts at 1. Use [start_line, -1] to show all lines from `start_line` to the end.

concise.description: Optional for the `view` command. If `True`, displays a concise skeletal view of the file. Very useful for localization tasks. Highly recommended for large files.

"""
Script to reproduce the issue with autoreloading of dotted module names.

The issue is that when running `python -m foo.bar.baz`, the autoreloader
incorrectly ends up using `-m foo.bar` instead of `-m foo.bar.baz`.
"""
import sys
import tempfile
import types
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

# Add the testbed to sys.path so we can import django
sys.path.insert(0, '/testbed')

from django.utils import autoreload

def test_dotted_module_name():
    """Test the current behavior with dotted module names."""
    
    # Create a mock module that simulates running python -m foo.bar.baz
    mock_module = types.ModuleType('__main__')
    mock_module.__spec__ = types.SimpleNamespace()
    # This simulates what happens when you run python -m foo.bar.baz
    # __spec__.name would be 'foo.bar.bz' but __spec__.parent would be 'foo.bar'
    mock_module.__spec__.name = 'foo.bar.baz'
    mock_module.__spec__.parent = 'foo.bar'
    
    with mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, {'__main__': mock_module}):
        with mock.patch('sys.argv', ['-m', 'foo.bar.baz', 'runserver']):
            with mock.patch('sys.warnoptions', []):
                result = autoreload.get_child_arguments()
                print("Current result:", result)
                
                # The current implementation gives us ['-m', 'foo.bar', 'runserver']
                # But it should give us ['-m', 'foo.bar.baz', 'runserver']
                expected = [sys.executable, '-m', 'foo.bar.baz', 'runserver']
                print("Expected result:", expected)
                
                if result == expected:
                    print("✅ PASS: Correct module path used")
                    return True
                else:
                    print("❌ FAIL: Incorrect module path used")
                    print(f"Got: {result}")
                    print(f"Expected: {expected}")
                    return False

def test_simple_module_name():
    """Test that simple module names still work correctly."""
    
    # Create a mock module that simulates running python -m foo.bar
    mock_module = types.ModuleType('__main__')
    mock_module.__spec__ = types.SimpleNamespace()
    # This simulates what happens when you run python -m foo.bar
    # __spec__.name would be 'foo.bar' and __spec__.parent would be 'foo'
    mock_module.__spec__.name = 'foo.bar'
    mock_module.__spec__.parent = 'foo'
    
    with mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, {'__main__': mock_module}):
        with mock.patch('sys.argv', ['-m', 'foo.bar', 'runserver']):
            with mock.patch('sys.warnoptions', []):
                result = autoreload.get_child_arguments()
                print("\nSimple module test result:", result)
                
                expected = [sys.executable, '-m', 'foo.bar', 'runserver']
                print("Expected result:", expected)
                
                if result == expected:
                    print("✅ PASS: Simple module path works correctly")
                    return True
                else:
                    print("❌ FAIL: Simple module path failed")
                    return False

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print("Testing autoreloader with dotted module names...")
    
    # Test the current broken behavior
    dotted_success = test_dotted_module_name()
    simple_success = test_simple_module_name()
    
    if not dotted_success:
        print("\n🐛 The issue is confirmed: dotted module names don't work correctly")
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("\n✅ All tests passed!")
        sys.exit(0)"}

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The command to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `undo_edit`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/testbed/file.py` or `/testbed`.

file_text.description: Required for the `create` command, contains the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required for the `str_replace` command, specifies the string in `path` to replace.

new_str.description: Optional for the `str_replace` command to specify the replacement string. Required for the `insert` command to specify the string to insert.

insert_line.description: Required for the `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line specified.

view_range.description: Optional for the `view` command when `path` points to a file. Specifies the line range to view. E.g., [11, 12] shows lines 11 and 12. Indexing starts at 1. Use [start_line, -1] to show all lines from `start_line` to the end.

concise.description: Optional for the `view` command. If `True`, displays a concise skeletal view of the file. Very useful for localization tasks. Highly recommended for large files.

Can you run a quick SOC 2 Type II readiness checklist for a 40-person B2B SaaS? Stack: AWS (EKS, RDS Postgres, S3), Okta SSO, GitHub Actions, Slack, Google Workspace, Jira/Confluence. Known gaps: no formal risk register, no comprehensive asset inventory, ad-hoc change management, and sparse vendor reviews. Please provide a concise checklist aligned to Security, Availability, and Confidentiality; then list likely gaps and a prioritized 30/60/90-day remediation plan.

Here’s a concise SOC 2 Type II readiness checklist tailored to your stack, followed by likely gaps and a 30/60/90-day plan.

Condensed audit checklist (Security, Availability, Confidentiality)
- Governance & risk management
  - Check: Approved policies (security, risk, access, change, incident, vendor), annual review, training. Evidence: policy PDFs with approvals, training logs.
  - Check: Risk assessment + register, control owners, TSC mapping. Evidence: risk register, control matrix.
- Asset & data management
  - Check: Central inventory (AWS accounts/resources, endpoints, repos, SaaS apps), data classification, data flows, retention/disposal. Evidence: inventory export, classification standard, data-flow diagram.
- Access control (Okta/AWS/GitHub)
  - Check: SSO+MFA enforced, least privilege RBAC, JML process, quarterly access reviews, break-glass accounts, key/secret management. Evidence: Okta policies/exports, IAM role matrix, access review sign-offs, KMS/secret store configs.
- Change management (GitHub Actions/IaC)
  - Check: Change policy, ticket linkage, peer review, protected branches, environment approvals, emergency change log, segregation of duties. Evidence: sample PRs, branch rules, env protection settings, change tickets.
- Secure SDLC & vulnerability management
  - Check: SCA/SAST/DAST/container scans, patch SLAs, findings triage/tracking, annual pen test. Evidence: scanner reports, vuln dashboard, Jira tickets, pen-test report.
- Logging, monitoring, incident response
  - Check: Centralized logs (CloudTrail, EKS/app), retention, alerting, IR policy/runbooks, tabletop exercises. Evidence: SIEM config, alert screenshots, incident records.
- Availability & resilience
  - Check: RTO/RPO defined, backups and restore tests (RDS/S3), HA configs, capacity monitoring, DR plan/drills. Evidence: backup/restore logs, failover report, uptime metrics.
- Vendor/third-party management
  - Check: Vendor inventory, risk tiering, DPAs, SOC/ISO evidence, annual reviews, offboarding. Evidence: inventory, review worksheets, contracts.
- Endpoint & physical
  - Check: MDM, disk encryption, screen lock, AV/EDR; office access controls if applicable. Evidence: MDM compliance export, endpoint policy.
- Confidentiality controls
  - Check: Encryption in transit/at rest, KMS rotation, secrets management, masking in non-prod, NDAs. Evidence: KMS key policy/rotation, TLS settings, secret vault config.

Likely gaps from your notes (and quick wins)
- Missing risk register → Stand up a lightweight register (risk, owner, likelihood/impact, treatment, due date); review monthly; map to TSC.
- No comprehensive asset inventory → Aggregate AWS (Organizations/Config), Okta apps, GitHub repos, endpoints (MDM), SaaS apps into one source; assign owners and criticality.
- Ad-hoc change management → Publish change policy; require PR + one reviewer; link Jira issue to PR; enforce protected branches and GitHub Actions environment approvals; add emergency change template and weekly review.
- Sparse vendor reviews → Build vendor inventory and tiering; collect SOC 2/ISO or DPAs; document reviews and compensating controls for gaps.
- Common adjacent gaps to check: documented JML, quarterly access reviews, incident runbooks/tabletop evidence, restore test evidence, vuln SLAs and scan coverage, data classification and data-flow diagrams, DR drill results, evidence retention schedule.

Prioritized remediation plan (90 days)
- Days 0–30
  - Publish core policies (security, access, change, IR, vendor, risk) with approvals; roll out training.
  - Create risk register; hold first review; assign owners and treatments.
  - Baseline inventory: AWS resources, Okta apps/groups, GitHub repos, SaaS, endpoints; name owners.
  - Enforce SSO+MFA everywhere; tighten admin RBAC and break-glass controls.
  - Implement change policy: PR + reviewer rules; require ticket links; enable environment protections in GitHub Actions.
  - Vendor inventory + DPAs; request SOC/ISO reports from critical vendors.
  - Centralize logging (org CloudTrail, EKS/app logs to SIEM/log bucket) with retention.
- Days 31–60
  - Publish data classification standard; build system data-flow diagrams.
  - Run first quarterly access reviews (Okta, AWS/IAM, DB, GitHub) and document results.
  - Establish vulnerability management: enable SCA/SAST/container scanning; define severity SLAs; track in Jira.
  - Perform and document an RDS restore test; validate RPO/RTO assumptions.
  - Draft IR runbooks; run a tabletop and capture minutes and lessons.
- Days 61–90
  - Finalize DR plan; conduct a partial failover or restore-based drill; record metrics vs. RTO/RPO.
  - Consolidate secrets management and define KMS key rotation schedule; mask sensitive data in non-prod.
  - Complete vendor risk reviews and compensating controls matrix for missing attestations.
  - Perform an internal control self-audit and assemble the evidence binder for auditor readiness.

Evidence to start collecting
- Approved policies and training logs
- Risk register snapshot and review minutes
- Asset inventory exports and owner lists
- Access review sign-offs and JML records
- Change samples with PR approvals and tickets
- Scan reports and remediation tickets with SLA metrics
- Backup/restore logs and DR drill report
- Incident runbooks and tabletop minutes
- Vendor review worksheets, DPAs, SOC/ISO reports

If you share any current policies or sample evidence, I can tailor the checklist and plan further.

- Green: ≥80% on-time; ≤5% overdue; no Critical open >7 days; closure trend improving
